It is also said that the ahqab is a time for their drinking the boiling water and the ghassaq; when they are finished, there will be another kind of punishment for them.

Al-Suddi said: the huqb is seventy years.

Bashir ibn Ka'b said: three hundred years.

Ibn 'Umar said: forty years. It is also said: thirty thousand years.

Al-Hasan said: none of you knows what the ahqab are, but they mentioned that they are a hundred huqb, and one huqb of them is seventy thousand years, a day of them being like a thousand years.

It is also said that the verse is to be understood as applying to the sinners who will come out of the Fire. The first view that we mentioned is preferable, namely that the verse's intent is eternity, not limitation.

Al-Wahidi related from al-Hasan that he said: "By Allah, it is nothing but that when one huqb passes, another enters, then another, and so on forever."

The clause ﴿They will not taste therein any coolness or drink, except boiling water and ghassaq﴾ is a resumptive sentence explaining what the previous clause contains: that they will not taste in Hell, or during the ahqab, any coolness that would benefit them from its heat, nor any drink that would benefit them from their thirst, except hamim, which is boiling water, and ghassaq, which is the pus of the people of the Fire.

It may be in the accusative position as a circumstantial state of the pronoun of the tagheen, or an attribute of the ahqab. The exception is disjunct according to those who take bard to mean sleep. It may also be conjunct, from His saying ﴿drink﴾.

Mujahid, al-Suddi, Abu 'Ubayda, al-Kisa'i, al-Fadl ibn Khalid and Abu Mu'adh al-Nahwi said: the bard mentioned in this verse is sleep, and from it is the saying of al-Kindi:

*Her cheeks grew cool upon me, so the cold kept me*
*away from her and from kissing her, the cold.*

That is, sleep.

Al-Zajjaj said: that is, they will not taste therein the coolness of wind, nor shade, nor sleep, so bard is made to include these matters.

Al-Hasan, 'Ata' and Ibn Zayd said: bardan means rawh (comfort) and rawahah (relief).

The majority read ghassaqan with light pronunciation. Hamza and al-Kisa'i read it with the doubled sin. Its explanation and the explanation of hamim, and the difference of readings concerning them, have already been mentioned in Surah Sad.

﴿A fitting recompense.﴾ That is, in accordance with their deeds. Jaza' is in the accusative as a verbal noun, and wifaqan is its attribute.

Al-Farra' and al-Akhfash said: we recompensed them with a recompense that matched their deeds. Al-Zajjaj said: they were recompensed with a recompense that matched their deeds.

Al-Farra' said: al-wifaq is the plural of al-wafq, and al-wafq and al-muwafiq are one.

Muqatil said: the punishment matched the sin; there is no sin greater than evil, and no punishment greater than the Fire.

Al-Hasan and 'Ikrimah said: their deeds were evil, so Allah brought them what would hurt them.

﴿Indeed, they did not expect a reckoning.﴾ That is, they did not expect the reward of a reckoning.

Al-Zajjaj said: they did not believe in the resurrection, so they did not hope for their reckoning. The clause is a justification for their deserving the mentioned recompense.

﴿And they denied Our signs with vehement denial.﴾ That is, they denied the Quranic verses, or they denied what is more general than them, with intense denial. Fi'ial is from the verbal nouns of the tafa''ul form.

Al-Farra' said: it is an eloquent Yemeni dialect; one says kadhdhabtu kidhdhaban and kharraqtu al-qamis kharraqan.

Al-Jawhari said in al-Sihah: "and they denied Our signs with kidhdhaban" is one of the verbal nouns of the doubled form, because its verbal noun may come as taf'il like al-takleem, as fi'al like kidhdhab, as taf'ilah like tawsiyah, and as mufa''al like "And We tore them to shreds, every shred" [Saba: 19]. The majority read kidhdhaban with doubling.

Ali ibn Abi Talib read it with light pronunciation.

Abu 'Ali al-Farisi said: the light and the doubled forms are both the verbal noun of al-mukadhabah (denial).

Ibn 'Umar read kuddhaban with a damma on the kaf and doubling, as the plural of kadhib.

Abu Hatim said: its accusative is circumstantial.

Al-Zamakhshari said: it may also (meaning in this reading) mean the one who is eloquent in lying, as you say rajulun kaddhab like your saying hassan and bakhhal.

﴿And everything We have enumerated in a record.﴾ The majority read wa-kulla with the accusative by the construction of suppression: that is, "And We have enumerated everything We have enumerated."

Abu al-Simak read it with the nominative as an inceptive, and what follows is its predicate, and this clause is interposed between the cause and its effect. The accusative of kitaban is a verbal noun for ahsaynahu, since ahsaynahu has the meaning of kataba-nahu (We wrote it). It is also said it is accusative as a circumstantial state: that is, written. It is said the meaning is what We wrote in the Preserved Tablet so that the angels would know it. It is said it means what the guardian angels wrote concerning the deeds of the servants. It is also said it means knowledge, since what is written is further from being forgotten. The first is preferable, given His saying: ﴿And everything We have enumerated in a clear record﴾ [Ya-Sin: 12].

﴿So taste, for We will not increase you except in punishment.﴾ This clause is causally linked to their disbelief and denial of the signs.

Al-Razi said: this fa' is for the recompense, indicating that the command to taste is grounded in the previously explained evil of their deeds. Among the increase in their punishment is that whenever their skins are burned, Allah replaces them with other skins, and whenever the fire subsides, Allah increases them in blaze.

Ibn Mardawayh related from Ibn 'Abbas concerning ﴿about the great news﴾ that he said: it is the Quran. This is also narrated from a group of the Successors.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from him concerning His saying ﴿and We made a blazing lamp﴾ that he said: shining. ﴿And We sent down from the rain-clouds﴾ he said: the clouds. ﴿Water pouring forth﴾ he said: poured out.

Abd ibn Humayd, Abu Ya'la, Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir also related from him concerning ﴿pouring forth﴾ that he said: poured out.

Al-Shafi'i, Sa'id ibn Mansur, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh related from Ibn Mas'ud concerning His saying ﴿And We sent down from the rain-clouds water pouring forth﴾ that he said: Allah sends the wind, and it carries the water, and the clouds pass over it and are milked like a milch camel is milked. The pouring water descends from the sky like great drops, and the winds scatter it so that it falls in scattered form.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Anbari in al-Masahif related from Qatadah that he said: in the reading of Ibn 'Abbas, "And We sent down from the rain-clouds by the winds."

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from him concerning His saying ﴿And gardens of thick foliage﴾ that he said: intertwined.

Ibn Jarir also related from him concerning the verse that he said: he says: some of it has entwined with others.

Ibn al-Mundhir also related from him concerning His saying ﴿And the mountains will be set in motion and will become a mirage﴾ that he said: the mirage of the sun, which is the shimmering.

Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated from him (Ibn Abbas) regarding ﴿lābithīna fīhā aḥqābā﴾ (﴿remaining therein for ages﴾) that he said: "Years."

ʿAbd al-Razzaq, al-Firyabi, Hannad, ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Salim ibn Abi al-Jaʿd, who said: ʿAli ibn Abi Talib asked Hilal al-Hajari: "What do you find the ḥuqb (an extremely long, indefinite span of time) to be in the Book of Allah?" He replied: "We find it to be eighty years, each year consisting of twelve months, each month thirty days, and each day a thousand years."

Saʿid ibn Mansur and al-Hakim, who authenticated it, narrated from Ibn Masʿud regarding the verse that he said: "One ḥuqb is eighty years."

al-Bazzar narrated from Abu Hurayra, traced back to the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "The ḥuqb is eighty years, a year is three hundred and sixty days, and a day is like a thousand years of what you count."

ʿAbd ibn Humayd narrated from him (Abu Hurayra) that he said: "The ḥuqb is eighty years, a day of which is like a sixth of the world."

Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh narrated...

al-Suyuti said: With a weak chain, from Abu Umama, from the Prophet (ﷺ) regarding ﴿lābithīna fīhā aḥqābā﴾, he said: "The ḥuqb is a thousand months, a month is thirty days, and a year is twelve months, three hundred and sixty days, each day of which is a thousand years of what you count. So the ḥuqb is thirty thousand years."

al-Bazzar, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Daylami narrated from Ibn Umar, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "By Allah, whoever enters the Fire will not leave it until he remains in it for ages. The ḥuqb is some eighty years, each year is three hundred and sixty days, and each day is a thousand years of what you count."

Ibn Umar said: "So let no one rely on the belief that he will leave the Fire."

Saʿid ibn Mansur and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Abdullah ibn Amr who said: "One ḥuqb is eighty years."

Ibn Jarir narrated from Ibn Abbas the same.

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ubada ibn al-Samit who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The ḥuqb is forty years."

Ibn Jarir narrated from Khalid ibn Maʿdan regarding His saying ﴿lābithīna fīhā aḥqābā﴾ and His saying ﴿illā mā shāʾa rabbuka﴾ (﴿except what your Lord wills﴾), that both apply to the people of monotheism among the people of the qiblah.

ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Masʿud who said: "The zamharir (extreme cold) of Hell is part of their punishment, because Allah says: ﴿lā yadhūqūna fīhā bardan wa-lā sharāban﴾ (﴿they will not taste therein any coolness or drink﴾)."

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Abu Hurayra, from the Prophet (ﷺ), regarding His saying ﴿lā yadhūqūna fīhā bardan wa-lā sharāban illā ḥamīman﴾ (﴿they will not taste therein any coolness or drink, except boiling water﴾), he said: "Its heat has reached its limit," and ﴿wa-ghassāqan﴾ (﴿and dark, pus-like fluid﴾): "Its heat has reached its limit. When a man brings the vessel to his mouth, the skin of his face falls off, until only bones remain, rattling."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding ﴿jazāʾan wifāqā﴾ (﴿a fitting recompense﴾) that he said: "It corresponded to their deeds."

ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Abdullah ibn Amr who said: "No verse was ever revealed concerning the people of the Fire more severe than this: ﴿fadhūqū falan nazīdakum illā ʿadhāban﴾ (﴿So taste, and We will not increase you except in punishment﴾). They will be in ever-increasing punishment from Allah forever."

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 78, verses 31–40 (part 1 of 2):

His saying: ﴿Indeed, for the righteous there is a triumph (mafaz)﴾. This begins the description of the condition of the believers and what Allah has prepared for them of good, after the description of the condition of the disbelievers and what Allah has prepared for them of evil. Al-mafaz is a verbal noun meaning the success, the attainment of a blessing and an objective, and deliverance from the Fire. From it comes the saying that the desert is called mafazah, optimistically, for the escape from it.

Then Allah, glorified is He, explained this mafaz, saying: ﴿gardens and grapevines﴾. Both are in the accusative case, either as a badal (substitution) for mafazan, a badal al-ishtimal (substitution of inclusion), or a badal kull min kull (total substitution) by way of emphasis, making these very things a mafaza. It is also permissible that the accusative is by the implied verb a'ni ("I mean"). If mafazan means "success," then an omitted genitive construction is presumed, i.e., "the success of gardens." Hada'iq is the plural of hadiqah, which is an enclosed orchard; a'nab is the plural of inab, i.e., vineyards of grapes.

﴿And maidens of equal age (kawa'ib atraban)﴾. Al-kawa'ib is the plural of ka'ibah, meaning one whose breasts are firm (nahidah). It is said: the girl kaabat takaabu ta'kiban and ku'ublan, and nahadat tanhadu nuhudan. The meaning is that they are women whose breasts have become firm and rounded, i.e., their breasts became like knuckles (ka'b) on their chests.

Al-Dahhak said: al-kawa'ib are virgins (al-adhara).

Qays ibn Asim said:
"And how many a chaste (noble) woman we have possessed, and how many a firm-breasted girl who knew not the hardship of the pressing (one who has reached puberty)."

And Umar ibn Abi Rabi'ah said:
"My shield, beyond what I feared, was three figures: firm-breasted maidens and one who has reached puberty."

Al-atrab are peers in age, and its investigation has already been given in surat al-Baqarah.

﴿And a cup overflowing (dihaqan)﴾, i.e., full.

Al-Hasan, Qatadah and Ibn Zayd said: that is, brimming and filled. It is said: adhqatu al-ka's, meaning I filled the cup. From this is the saying of the poet:
"Ah, give me to drink pure, may the one who pours it give you drink, from its water in your full cup."

Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Ikrimah and Mujahid said: dihaqan means successive, one following another.

Zayd ibn Aslam said: dihaqan means pure.

Al-kas means the known vessel, and it is not called a cup (kas) unless there is drink in it.

﴿They will not hear therein any idle talk or lying (kidhdhaban)﴾, i.e., they will not hear in Paradise any idle talk, which is falsehood in speech, nor kidhdhaban: that is, they will not deny one another.

The majority read kidhdhaban with shaddah (doubling), while al-Kisa'i read it here with the lightened form (kidhaban), and agreed with the majority on the doubled form in His saying: ﴿And they denied Our signs with (full) denial (kidhdhaban)﴾, mentioned earlier in this surah, because the verb is explicit there. We have already mentioned the disagreement over kidhdhaban: whether it is from the verbal nouns of tafil or of mufa'alah.

﴿As a reward from your Lord﴾, i.e., He recompensed them with what has been mentioned as a reward.

Al-Zajjaj said: the meaning is "He rewarded them with a reward"; likewise ata' (gift), i.e., and He gave them a gift, hisaban. Abu Ubaydah said: sufficient.

Ibn Qutaybah said: abundant. It is said: ahsabtu fulanan, meaning I gave a person abundant gift, and from it is the saying of the poet:
"We give the young man of the tribe if he is hungry, and we make him sufficed (nuhsibuhu) if he is not hungry."

Ibn Qutaybah said: that is, we give him until he says "enough for me" (hasbi).

Al-Zajjaj said: hisaban means what suffices them.

Al-Akhfash said: it is said ahsabani kadha, meaning it sufficed me.

Al-Kalbi said: He reckoned with them and gave them, for a good deed, ten.

Mujahid said: hisaban for what they did, so hisab here means measure: i.e., He determines what is due to them according to the promise of the Lord, glorified is He, for He promised ten for a good deed, and promised seven hundred-fold for some, and promised to some a reward without end or measure, as in His saying: ﴿Only those who are patient will be given their reward without account﴾ [al-Zumar: 10]. Abu Hashim read hassaban with a fatha on the ha and shaddah on the sin, meaning sufficient.

Al-Asma'i said: the Arabs say: hassabtu al-rajul with shaddah, when I honored him, and from it is the saying of the poet:
"When his guest comes to him, he gives him (yuhsibuhu) abundantly."

Ibn Abbas read hisanan with the nun.

﴿Lord of the heavens and the earth and what is between them, the Most Merciful﴾.

Ibn Mas'ud, Nafi', Abu Amr, Ibn Kathir, Zayd from Ya'qub, and al-Mufaddal from Asim read rabbu and al-Rahman with raf' (nominative), on the basis that rabbu is a mubtada' (subject) and al-Rahman its khabar (predicate), or that rabbu is the khabar of an implied mubtada', i.e., "He is the Lord," and al-Rahman is its sifah (attribute), and la yamlikuna is the khabar of rabbu. Or that rabbu is a mubtada', al-Rahman a second mubtada', and la yamlikuna the khabar of the second mubtada', the whole sentence being the khabar of the first.

Ya'qub in one narration, Ibn Amir, and Asim in one narration read both with genitive case, on the basis that rabbi is a badal (substitute) for rabbika and al-Rahman a sifah of it.

Ibn Abbas, Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read the first in the genitive as badal, and the second in the nominative as the khabar of an omitted mubtada', i.e., "He is al-Rahman." Abu Ubaydah chose this reading and said: this reading is the most just, so rabbi is genitive because it is near rabbika, making it a description of Him, and al-Rahman is nominative because it is distant from it, by way of resumption (isti'naf). Its khabar is ﴿they have no power to address Him (la yamlikuna minhu khitaban)﴾, i.e., they have no power to ask except in what He has permitted them. Al-Kisa'i said: they have no power to address Him with intercession except by His permission. It is said that khitab means speech: i.e., they have no power to address the Lord, glorified is He, except by His permission. Its evidence is ﴿No soul shall speak except by His permission﴾ [Hud: 105]. It is said that it refers to the disbelievers, while the believers intercede.

It is permissible that this sentence be in the accusative position as a hal (circumstantial clause), as explained earlier, and it is permissible that it be a resumed sentence confirming what the lordship implies of greatness and majesty.

﴿On the Day when the Spirit and the angels stand in ranks (saffan)﴾. The time-phrase is in the accusative governed by la yatakallamuna or by la yamlikuna. Saffan is in the accusative as a hal: i.e., lined up, or as a verbal noun: i.e., they arrange themselves in rows. His saying la yatakallamuna is in the accusative position as a hal, or is a resumed sentence establishing what precedes it.

The meaning of "the Spirit" has been disputed. It is said that it is an angel greater than the seven heavens, the seven earths and the mountains. It is said it is Jibril; this was said by al-Sha'bi, al-Dahhak and Sa'id ibn Jubayr.

It is said that the Ruh are a host of Allah's hosts who are not angels; this was said by Abu Salih and Mujahid. It is said they are the noblest of the angels; this was said by Muqatil ibn Hayyan.

It is said they are guardians over the angels; this was said by Ibn Abi Najih.

It is said they are the children of Adam; this was said by al-Hasan and Qatadah.

It is said they are the spirits of the children of Adam who stand in rows, while the angels stand in rows, and that is between the two blasts, before they are returned to bodies; this was said by Atiyyah al-Awfi.

It is said it is the Qur'an; this was said by Zayd ibn Aslam.

His saying ﴿except him whom the Most Merciful has permitted﴾ may be a badal from the pronoun in yatakallamuna, or may be in the accusative on the original basis of exception. The meaning: they will not intercede for anyone except him whom the Most Merciful has permitted to intercede; or they will not speak except on behalf of one whom the Most Merciful has permitted, and that person was among those who said what is right (sawaban). Al-Dahhak and Mujahid said: "sawaban" means truth (haqqan).

Abu Salih said: "There is no god but Allah."

The root of sawab is correctness (sadad) of speech and action.

It is said: "They will not speak" refers to the angels and the Spirit who stood in rows out of awe and reverence, except him whom the Most Merciful has permitted among them to intercede, and they have said what is right.

Al-Hasan said: the Spirit will stand on the Day of Resurrection; no one enters Paradise except through the Spirit, and no one enters the Fire except through deeds.

Al-Wahidi said: "They will not speak" refers to all creation except him whom the Most Merciful has permitted, and they are the believers and the angels. "Said what is right in the world" means he bore witness to tawhid.

The indication in His saying ﴿That﴾ refers to the Day of their standing in that description. It is a mubtada' whose khabar is ﴿the True Day (al-yawm al-haqq)﴾, i.e., the occurring, the realized, the certain. ﴿So whoever wills, let him take toward his Lord a return (ma'aban)﴾, i.e., a place of return to which he returns by righteous deeds; for when he does good, it brings him near to Allah, and when he does evil, it distances him from Him. The meaning of "toward his Lord" is toward the reward of his Lord. Qatadah said: ma'aban means a way.

Then Allah, glorified is He, increased the warning to the disbelievers, saying: ﴿Indeed, We have warned you of a near punishment﴾, meaning the punishment in the Hereafter, and everything that is coming is near. Similar is His saying: ﴿As if they, on the Day they see it, had not remained but an evening or its morning﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 46]. Thus said al-Kalbi and others.

Ibn Jarir transmitted from Ibn Mas'ud: he said, "The Spirit is in the fourth heaven, and it is greater than the heavens and the mountains and the angels. Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir in al-Asma' wa al-Sifat transmitted from him also, regarding ﴿and said what is right﴾: he said, "There is no god but Allah."

Qatadah said: it is the punishment of this world, because it is the nearer of the two punishments.

Muqatil said: it is the killing of Quraysh at Badr. The first is preferable because of His saying: ﴿and the disbeliever will say, "Would that I were dust!"﴾, for "the disbeliever" stands in contrast to "al-mar'." The meaning is the class of disbeliever who wishes he were dust, because of what he witnesses of the kinds of punishment Allah has prepared for him. The meaning is that he wishes he had been dust in the world and had not been created, or dust on the Day of Resurrection.

It is said the disbeliever is Abu Jahl; it is said Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Asad al-Makhzumi; it is said Iblis. The first is preferable in view of the generality of the wording, and the specificity of the occasion does not negate it, as has been mentioned more than once.

Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim (who authenticated it), Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi have transmitted from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying ﴿and a cup overflowing﴾: he said, "It is the full, brimming, successive one." Then he recited ﴿On the Day when the Spirit and the angels stand in ranks﴾ and said: "These are a host and these are a host."

Ibn Jarir transmitted from Ibn Mas'ud: he said, "The Spirit is in the fourth heaven, and it is greater than the heavens and the mountains and the angels. It glorifies twelve thousand glorifications each day; Allah creates from each glorification an angel, who will come on the Day of Resurrection in one row."

Abu al-Shaykh transmitted from Ibn Abbas: he said, "Indeed Jibril, on the Day of Resurrection, will stand before the Almighty, his limbs trembling from fear of Allah's punishment, saying: 'Glory be to You, there is no god but You; we did not worship You as You deserve to be worshipped,' and the distance between his shoulders is as the distance between east and west. Have you not heard the saying of Allah: ﴿On the Day when the Spirit and the angels stand in ranks﴾?"

Al-Bayhaqi in al-Asma' wa al-Sifat transmitted from him regarding ﴿the Day when the Spirit stands﴾: he said, "It means the time when the spirits of people stand, from among the angels, between the two blasts, before the spirits are returned to the bodies."

Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir in al-Asma' wa al-Sifat transmitted from him also, regarding ﴿and said what is right﴾: he said, "There is no god but Allah."

Ibn Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Bayhaqi in (al-Ba'th wa'l-Nushur) narrated from Abu Hurayrah, who said: "All of creation will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection: the beasts, the animals, the birds, and everything else. The punishment of Allah will reach such a degree that the hornless sheep will be taken to account on behalf of the horned ones. Then He will say: 'Be dust!' And that is when the disbeliever will say: ﴿Would that I were dust!﴾"

Al-mafaz is a verbal noun meaning the success, the attainment of a blessing and an objective, and deliverance from the Fire. From it comes the saying that the desert is called mafazah, optimistically, for the escape from it.

Then Allah, glorified is He, explained this mafaz, saying: ﴿gardens and grapevines﴾. Both are in the accusative case, either as a badal (substitution) for mafazan, a badal al-ishtimal (substitution of inclusion), or a badal kull min kull (total substitution) by way of emphasis, making these very things a mafaza. It is also permissible that the accusative is by the implied verb a'ni ("I mean"). If mafazan means "success," then an omitted genitive construction is presumed, i.e., "the success of gardens." Hada'iq is the plural of hadiqah, which is an enclosed orchard; a'nab is the plural of inab, i.e., vineyards of grapes.

﴿And maidens of equal age (kawa'ib atraban)﴾. Al-kawa'ib is the plural of ka'ibah, meaning one whose breasts are firm (nahidah). It is said: the girl kaabat takaabu ta'kiban and ku'ublan, and nahadat tanhadu nuhudan. The meaning is that they are women whose breasts have become firm and rounded, i.e., their breasts became like knuckles (ka'b) on their chests.

Al-Dahhak said: al-kawa'ib are virgins (al-adhara).

Qays ibn Asim said:
"And how many a chaste (noble) woman we have possessed, and how many a firm-breasted girl who knew not the hardship of the pressing (one who has reached puberty)."

And Umar ibn Abi Rabi'ah said:
"My shield, beyond what I feared, was three figures: firm-breasted maidens and one who has reached puberty."

Al-atrab are peers in age, and its investigation has already been given in surat al-Baqarah.

﴿And a cup overflowing (dihaqan)﴾, i.e., full.

Al-Hasan, Qatadah and Ibn Zayd said: that is, brimming and filled. It is said: adhqatu al-ka's, meaning I filled the cup. From this is the saying of the poet:
"Ah, give me to drink pure, may the one who pours it give you drink, from its water in your full cup."

Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Ikrimah and Mujahid said: dihaqan means successive, one following another.

Zayd ibn Aslam said: dihaqan means pure.

Al-kas means the known vessel, and it is not called a cup (kas) unless there is drink in it.

﴿They will not hear therein any idle talk or lying (kidhdhaban)﴾, i.e., they will not hear in Paradise any idle talk, which is falsehood in speech, nor kidhdhaban: that is, they will not deny one another.

The majority read kidhdhaban with shaddah (doubling), while al-Kisa'i read it here with the lightened form (kidhaban), and agreed with the majority on the doubled form in His saying: ﴿And they denied Our signs with (full) denial (kidhdhaban)﴾, mentioned earlier in this surah, because the verb is explicit there. We have already mentioned the disagreement over kidhdhaban: whether it is from the verbal nouns of tafil or of mufa'alah.

﴿As a reward from your Lord﴾, i.e., He recompensed them with what has been mentioned as a reward.

Al-Zajjaj said: the meaning is "He rewarded them with a reward"; likewise ata' (gift), i.e., and He gave them a gift, hisaban. Abu Ubaydah said: sufficient.

Ibn Qutaybah said: abundant. It is said: ahsabtu fulanan, meaning I gave a person abundant gift, and from it is the saying of the poet:
"We give the young man of the tribe if he is hungry, and we make him sufficed (nuhsibuhu) if he is not hungry."

Ibn Qutaybah said: that is, we give him until he says "enough for me" (hasbi).

Al-Zajjaj said: hisaban means what suffices them.

Al-Akhfash said: it is said ahsabani kadha, meaning it sufficed me.

Al-Kalbi said: He reckoned with them and gave them, for a good deed, ten.

Mujahid said: hisaban for what they did, so hisab here means measure: i.e., He determines what is due to them according to the promise of the Lord, glorified is He, for He promised ten for a good deed, and promised seven hundred-fold for some, and promised to some a reward without end or measure, as in His saying: ﴿Only those who are patient will be given their reward without account﴾ [al-Zumar: 10]. Abu Hashim read hassaban with a fatha on the ha and shaddah on the sin, meaning sufficient.

Al-Asma'i said: the Arabs say: hassabtu al-rajul with shaddah, when I honored him, and from it is the saying of the poet:
"When his guest comes to him, he gives him (yuhsibuhu) abundantly."

Ibn Abbas read hisanan with the nun.

﴿Lord of the heavens and the earth and what is between them, the Most Merciful﴾.

Ibn Mas'ud, Nafi', Abu Amr, Ibn Kathir, Zayd from Ya'qub, and al-Mufaddal from Asim read rabbu and al-Rahman with raf' (nominative), on the basis that rabbu is a mubtada' (subject) and al-Rahman its khabar (predicate), or that rabbu is the khabar of an implied mubtada', i.e., "He is the Lord," and al-Rahman is its sifah (attribute), and la yamlikuna is the khabar of rabbu. Al-Kisa'i said: they have no power to address Him with intercession except by His permission. It is said that khitab means speech: i.e., they have no power to address the Lord, glorified is He, except by His permission. Its evidence is ﴿No soul shall speak except by His permission﴾ [Hud: 105]. It is said that it refers to the disbelievers, while the believers intercede.

It is permissible that this sentence be in the accusative position as a hal (circumstantial clause), as explained earlier, and it is permissible that it be a resumed sentence confirming what the lordship implies of greatness and majesty.

﴿On the Day when the Spirit and the angels stand in ranks (saffan)﴾. The time-phrase is in the accusative governed by la yatakallamuna or by la yamlikuna. It is said that the Ruh are a host of Allah's hosts who are not angels; this was said by Abu Salih and Mujahid. It is said they are the noblest of the angels; this was said by Muqatil ibn Hayyan.

It is said they are guardians over the angels; this was said by Ibn Abi Najih.

It is said they are the children of Adam; this was said by al-Hasan and Qatadah.

It is said they are the spirits of the children of Adam who stand in rows, while the angels stand in rows, and that is between the two blasts, before they are returned to bodies; this was said by Atiyyah al-Awfi.

It is said it is the Qur'an; this was said by Zayd ibn Aslam.

The meaning: they will not intercede for anyone except him whom the Most Merciful has permitted to intercede; or they will not speak except on behalf of one whom the Most Merciful has permitted, and that person was among those who said what is right (sawaban). Al-Dahhak and Mujahid said: "sawaban" means truth (haqqan).

Abu Salih said: "There is no god but Allah."

The root of sawab is correctness (sadad) of speech and action.

It is said: "They will not speak" refers to the angels and the Spirit who stood in rows out of awe and reverence, except him whom the Most Merciful has permitted among them to intercede, and they have said what is right.

Al-Hasan said: the Spirit will stand on the Day of Resurrection; no one enters Paradise except through the Spirit, and no one enters the Fire except through deeds.

Al-Wahidi said: "They will not speak" refers to all creation except him whom the Most Merciful has permitted, and they are the believers and the angels. "Said what is right in the world" means he bore witness to tawhid.

The indication in His saying ﴿That﴾ refers to the Day of their standing in that description. It is a mubtada' whose khabar is ﴿the True Day (al-yawm al-haqq)﴾, i.e., the occurring, the realized, the certain. ﴿So whoever wills, let him take toward his Lord a return (ma'aban)﴾, i.e., a place of return to which he returns by righteous deeds; for when he does good, it brings him near to Allah, and when he does evil, it distances him from Him. The meaning of "toward his Lord" is toward the reward of his Lord. Qatadah said: ma'aban means a way.

Then Allah, glorified is He, increased the warning to the disbelievers, saying: ﴿Indeed, We have warned you of a near punishment﴾, meaning the punishment in the Hereafter, and everything that is coming is near. Similar is His saying: ﴿As if they, on the Day they see it, had not remained but an evening or its morning﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 46]. Thus said al-Kalbi and others.

Qatadah said: it is the punishment of this world, because it is the nearer of the two punishments.

Muqatil said: it is the killing of Quraysh at Badr. The first is preferable because of His saying: ﴿On the Day when a man sees what his hands have sent forward﴾, for the time-phrase is either a badal from "punishment" or a time-phrase governed by an implied verb which is an attribute of it: i.e., a punishment occurring ﴿on the Day when a man looks (yanzuru al-mar')﴾, i.e., witnesses what he has sent forward of good or evil. And "ma" is either a relative pronoun or an interrogative.

Al-Hasan said: "al-mar'" here is the believer: i.e., he finds his deed for himself. As for the disbeliever, he finds no deed for himself, so he wishes he were dust. It is said the meaning is the disbeliever in general; it is said it is Ubayy ibn Khalaf and Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'ayt. The first is preferable because of His saying: ﴿and the disbeliever will say, "Would that I were dust!"﴾, for "the disbeliever" stands in contrast to "al-mar'." The meaning is the class of disbeliever who wishes he were dust, because of what he witnesses of the kinds of punishment Allah has prepared for him. The meaning is that he wishes he had been dust in the world and had not been created, or dust on the Day of Resurrection.

It is said the disbeliever is Abu Jahl; it is said Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Asad al-Makhzumi; it is said Iblis. The first is preferable in view of the generality of the wording, and the specificity of the occasion does not negate it, as has been mentioned more than once.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bayhaqi have transmitted from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying ﴿Indeed for the righteous there is a triumph﴾: he said, "A place of recreation (muntazah)." Regarding ﴿kawa'ib﴾ he said, "Round-breasted," and ﴿atraban﴾ he said, "Of equal age." Regarding ﴿kasan dihaqan﴾ he said, "Full."

Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim (who authenticated it), Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi have transmitted from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying ﴿and a cup overflowing﴾: he said, "It is the full, brimming, successive one." Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from him ﴿dihaqan﴾: he said, "Successive (diraakan)."

Abd ibn Humayd also transmitted from him: he said, "If there is wine in it, it is a cup; if there is no wine in it, it is not a cup."

The meaning of "toward his Lord" is toward the reward of his Lord. Qatadah said: ma'aban means a way.

Then Allah, glorified is He, increased the warning to the disbelievers, saying: ﴿Indeed, We have warned you of a near punishment﴾, meaning the punishment in the Hereafter, and everything that is coming is near. Similar is His saying: ﴿As if they, on the Day they see it, had not remained but an evening or its morning﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 46]. Thus said al-Kalbi and others.

Qatadah said: it is the punishment of this world, because it is the nearer of the two punishments.

Muqatil said: it is the killing of Quraysh at Badr. The first is preferable because of His saying: ﴿On the Day when a man sees what his hands have sent forward﴾, for the time-phrase is either a badal from "punishment" or a time-phrase governed by an implied verb which is an attribute of it: i.e., a punishment occurring ﴿on the Day when a man looks (yanzuru al-mar')﴾, i.e., witnesses what he has sent forward of good or evil. And "ma" is either a relative pronoun or an interrogative.

Al-Hasan said: "al-mar'" here is the believer: i.e., he finds his deed for himself. As for the disbeliever, he finds no deed for himself, so he wishes he were dust. It is said the meaning is the disbeliever in general; it is said it is Ubayy ibn Khalaf and Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'ayt. The first is preferable because of His saying: ﴿and the disbeliever will say, "Would that I were dust!"﴾, for "the disbeliever" stands in contrast to "al-mar'." The meaning is the class of disbeliever who wishes he were dust, because of what he witnesses of the kinds of punishment Allah has prepared for him. The meaning is that he wishes he had been dust in the world and had not been created, or dust on the Day of Resurrection.

It is said the disbeliever is Abu Jahl; it is said Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Asad al-Makhzumi; it is said Iblis. The first is preferable in view of the generality of the wording, and the specificity of the occasion does not negate it, as has been mentioned more than once.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bayhaqi have transmitted from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying ﴿Indeed for the righteous there is a triumph﴾: he said, "A place of recreation (muntazah)." Regarding ﴿kawa'ib﴾ he said, "Round-breasted," and ﴿atraban﴾ he said, "Of equal age." Regarding ﴿kasan dihaqan﴾ he said, "Full."

Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim (who authenticated it), Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi have transmitted from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying ﴿and a cup overflowing﴾: he said, "It is the full, brimming, successive one." And I have often heard al-Abbas say: "O boy, give us to drink and fill (wadhqa) for us."

Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from him ﴿dihaqan﴾: he said, "Successive (diraakan)."

Abd ibn Humayd also transmitted from him: he said, "If there is wine in it, it is a cup; if there is no wine in it, it is not a cup."

Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh in al-Azamah, and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from him that the Prophet ﷺ said: "The Spirit is a host of Allah's hosts, not angels, having heads, hands and feet." Then he recited ﴿On the Day when the Spirit and the angels stand in ranks﴾ and said: "These are a host and these are a host."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Asma' wa al-Sifat transmitted from Ibn Abbas regarding ﴿the Day when the Spirit stands﴾: he said, "He is an angel, among the greatest of the angels in creation."

Ibn Jarir transmitted from Ibn Mas'ud: he said, "The Spirit is in the fourth heaven, and it is greater than the heavens and the mountains and the angels. It glorifies twelve thousand glorifications each day; Allah creates from each glorification an angel, who will come on the Day of Resurrection in one row."

Abu al-Shaykh transmitted from Ibn Abbas: he said, "Indeed Jibril, on the Day of Resurrection, will stand before the Almighty, his limbs trembling from fear of Allah's punishment, saying: 'Glory be to You, there is no god but You; we did not worship You as You deserve to be worshipped,' and the distance between his shoulders is as the distance between east and west. Have you not heard the saying of Allah: ﴿On the Day when the Spirit and the angels stand in ranks﴾?"

Al-Bayhaqi in al-Asma' wa al-Sifat transmitted from him regarding ﴿the Day when the Spirit stands﴾: he said, "It means the time when the spirits of people stand, from among the angels, between the two blasts, before the spirits are returned to the bodies."

Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir in al-Asma' wa al-Sifat transmitted from him also, regarding ﴿and said what is right﴾: he said, "There is no god but Allah."

Ibn Hamid, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Bayhaqi in (al-Ba'th wa'l-Nushur) narrated from Abu Hurayrah, who said: "All of creation will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection: the beasts, the animals, the birds, and everything else. The punishment of Allah will reach such a degree that the hornless sheep will be taken to account on behalf of the horned ones. Then He will say: 'Be dust!' And that is when the disbeliever will say: ﴿Would that I were dust!﴾"
